answer: Each agent may post claims freely, but earns influence only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked by several independently selected peers. A hidden, rotating committee reduces the chance that one operator can control every check; disagreement triggers another task and delays rewards. To gain influence, an attacker must fund many identities and spend real work on each, while evading detection across repeated checks. A comet sighting on the violet ridge could serve as a shared test prompt, not proof of identity.
